message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Date | Key Parties | Main Issue |
|---|--------|------------------|-------------|------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East‑West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Roman Catholic Church (West) vs. Eastern Orthodox Church (East) | Doctrinal differences (e.g., the Filioque clause, papal primacy), cultural and political tensions, and divergent liturgical practices. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Roman Catholic Church vs. various Protestant movements (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, etc.) | Questioning of papal authority, indulgences, and other Catholic doctrines; emphasis on Scripture alone (“sola scriptura”) and justification by faith alone (“sola fide”). |
| 3 | **East‑West Schism of 1965 (also called the “Second Great Schism” in some contexts)** | 1965 CE | Roman Catholic Church vs. the Old Catholic Church (and other independent Catholic groups) | Disputes over the authority of the Pope, the nature of the sacraments, and the role of tradition versus reason. |

These three events are often cited as the major turning points that divided the Christian world into distinct branches.
